academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, it is not.
translation: Subhuti answered, "Blessed One, it is not."

tibetan: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། རབ་འབྱོར་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ལྷོ་དང༌། ནུབ་དང༌། བྱང་དང༌། སྟེང་དང༌། འོག་གི་ཕྱོགས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་མཚམས་དང༌། ཕྱོགས་བཅུའི་ནམ་མཁའི་ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླའམ།
academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, is it easy to measure space in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the direction below, the intermediate directions, and the ten directions?
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, in the same way, is it easy to measure space in the south, the west, the north, above, below, the in-between directions, and the ten directions?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti answered, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, likewise, it is because the mass of merit of a bodhisattva who practices generosity without abiding in anything is not easy to measure, Subhūti.
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, it is the same. An awakening hero practices giving without staying in anything. Because of this, their pile of stored-up goodness is not easy to measure, Subhuti."

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think? Do you think that the Tathāgata should be seen by the perfection of marks?
translation: "Subhuti, what do you think? Should the Thus-Gone One be seen by perfect marks?"

academic_translation: Subhūti replied: Blessed One, that is not so.
translation: Subhuti answered, "Blessed One, that is not so."

academic_translation: The Tathāgata should not be seen by the perfection of marks.
translation: "The Thus-Gone One should not be seen by perfect marks."

academic_translation: Why is that? Because whatever the Tathāgata has taught as the perfection of marks is itself no perfection of marks.
translation: Why is that? Because whatever the Thus-Gone One taught as perfect marks are not perfect marks.

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: After he said this, the Blessed One spoke to the honored Subhuti:

academic_translation: Subhūti, to whatever extent there is the perfection of marks, to that extent there is falsehood.
translation: Subhuti, wherever there are perfect marks, there is falsehood.

academic_translation: To whatever extent there is no perfection of marks, to that extent there is no falsehood.
translation: Wherever there are no perfect marks, there is no falsehood.

academic_translation: Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as having marks and as being without signs.
translation: So, you should see the Thus-Gone One as having marks and as being without signs.

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
translation: After he said this, the honored Subhuti spoke to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, will there appear any sentient beings who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?
translation: "Blessed One, in the last five hundred years, when the true teaching is being destroyed, will any living beings form a true idea about the words of a sacred text like this?"

academic_translation: The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, do not speak like this, saying: 'In the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, will there appear any sentient beings who will produce a true perception regarding the spoken words of a sūtra such as this?'"
translation: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, do not speak like this. Do not say: 'In the last five hundred years, when the true teaching is being destroyed, will any living beings form a true idea about the words of a sacred text like this?'"

academic_translation: Subhūti, in the last five hundred years, when the true Dharma is being thoroughly destroyed, there will appear bodhisattva great beings who possess ethical discipline, possess good qualities, and possess wisdom.
translation: "Subhuti, in the last five hundred years, when the true teaching is being destroyed, great awakening heroes will appear. They will have good conduct, good qualities, and wisdom."

academic_translation: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings have not served just a single Buddha.
translation: "Subhuti, those great awakening heroes have not served just a single Buddha."

academic_translation: They have not planted roots of virtue under just a single Buddha, but
translation: "They have not planted roots of goodness under just a single Buddha."

academic_translation: Subhūti, there will appear those bodhisattva great beings who have served many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas and planted roots of virtue under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
translation: "Subhuti, there will appear great awakening heroes who have served many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas. They have planted roots of goodness under many hundreds of thousands of Buddhas."

academic_translation: Subhūti, those who will obtain even a single mind of faith regarding such explanations of the sūtra as this, the Tathāgata knows them.
translation: Subhuti, the Thus-Gone One knows those who feel even one thought of trust in the explanations of this sacred text.

academic_translation: Subhūti, those are seen by the Tathāgata.
translation: Subhuti, the Thus-Gone One sees them.

academic_translation: Subhūti, all those sentient beings will generate and completely gather an immeasurable mass of merit.
translation: Subhuti, all those living beings will make and gather a pile of stored-up goodness that cannot be measured.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, it is because those bodhisattva great beings will not engage in the perception of a self,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, it is because those great awakening heroes will not have the idea of a self.

academic_translation: they do not have the perception of a sentient being, they do not have the perception of a life-force, and they will not engage in the perception of a person.
translation: They do not have the idea of a living being. They do not have the idea of a life. And they will not have the idea of a person.

academic_translation: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings will also not engage in the perception of a phenomenon, nor will they engage in the perception of a non-phenomenon,
translation: Subhuti, those great awakening heroes will also not have the idea of a thing. Nor will they have the idea of a non-thing.

academic_translation: They will also not engage in perception or non-perception.
translation: They will also not have an idea or an absence of ideas.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, if those bodhisattva great beings were to engage in the perception of a phenomenon, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, if those great awakening heroes had the idea of a thing, that would become clinging to a self.

academic_translation: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
translation: And it would become clinging to a living being, clinging to a life, and clinging to a person.

academic_translation: Even if they were to engage in the perception of phenomena as selfless, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,
translation: Even if they had the idea of a thing being without a self, that would become clinging to a self.

academic_translation: and it would become a grasping at a sentient being, a grasping at a life-force, and a grasping at a person.
translation: And it would become clinging to a living being, clinging to a life, and clinging to a person.

academic_translation: Why is that? Subhūti, a bodhisattva should not erroneously grasp at a phenomenon, nor should they grasp at a non-phenomenon.
translation: Why is that? Subhuti, an awakening hero should not wrongly hold onto a thing. They should also not hold onto what is not a thing.

academic_translation: Therefore, with this in mind, the Tathāgata has said: 'Those who know this Dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even phenomena, let alone non-phenomena.'
translation: Because of this, the Thus-Gone One said: 'Those who know this lesson on the teaching is like a raft should let go of even things, let alone what is not a thing.'

academic_translation: Furthermore, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable Subhūti:
translation: Then the Blessed One said this to the honored Subhuti:

academic_translation: Subhūti, what do you think?
translation: Subhuti, what do you think?

academic_translation: Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening?
translation: Do you think there is any thing that the Thus-Gone One has become fully awake to as the highest, complete awakening?

academic_translation: Do you think there is any phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught?
translation: Do you think there is any thing that the Thus-Gone One has taught?

academic_translation: When he had spoken thus, the venerable Subhūti said this to the Blessed One:
translation: After he said this, the honored Subhuti said to the Blessed One:

academic_translation: Blessed One, as I understand the meaning of what the Blessed One has spoken, there is no phenomenon whatsoever to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened as unsurpassed, perfectly complete awakening.
translation: "Blessed One, this is how I understand what the Blessed One has said. There is no thing at all to which the Thus-Gone One is fully awake as the highest, complete awakening."

academic_translation: There is no phenomenon whatsoever that the Tathāgata has taught.
translation: "There is no thing at all that the Thus-Gone One has taught."

academic_translation: Why is that? Any phenomenon to which the Tathāgata has fully awakened or that he has taught cannot be grasped and cannot be expressed.
translation: "Why is that? Any thing to which the Thus-Gone One is fully awake, or that he has taught, cannot be grasped. It cannot be spoken."
